_comment: Palette. In /data rather than in code for the same reason the balance numbers are: it gets tuned, and art direction should not require touching the renderer. Section 6.1 makes readability a correctness requirement rather than a nicety, so from P1 armour classes must be distinguished by SHAPE as well as by colour - never colour alone.
_camera_comment: 3/4 orthographic, per master plan section 6.1. Orthographic rather than perspective so a platform reads the same wherever it sits on the board - with perspective, identical towers at the near and far edge look different sizes, which makes range and coverage harder to judge. Angles are in degrees; size is the vertical extent of the view in world units.

camera._comment: Perspective with a narrow field of view: narrow enough that a turret at the far edge is close to the same size as one at the near edge (the readability reason the camera was orthographic), wide enough to give real parallax and depth. Pitch is much shallower than before so you see the sides of things, which is most of what makes a scene read as 3D rather than as a diagram.

_world_comment: Heights are in world units on the Y axis; the simulation is flat and knows nothing about them. Scenery (trees, boulders, the ground mesh) is what the landscape is made of and it is the only part of the renderer whose cost scales with the SIZE of the board rather than with what is happening on it. Measured on a software rasteriser, which is a worst case and not a GPU: 57ms a frame before it, 91ms with it, 84ms with tree_shadows off. Draw calls stay flat at 35 from 25 entities to 400, which is the invariant that actually matters. If a real device ever struggles, tree_shadows is the first switch to reach for and tree_limit is the second.

world._enemy_class_colors: One colour per drone class, so the wave preview's armour grouping has a visual echo on the road: yellows/oranges are Light, greys/bronzes are Plated, and anything glowing cold is Shielded support. Hurt drones still lerp toward enemy_hurt.
world._shadow_budget: The shadow pass renders the whole scene a second time, and it is the most expensive thing in this game on a browser GPU. Trees are 5,000 instances and were casting; drones are hundreds. Both are switchable and tree_shadows is the first to give up - the board reads fine without treeline shadows and does not without turret ones.
world._render_scale: How many pixels the 3D pass is allowed. The web canvas resizes to the window times the display pixel ratio, so a HiDPI screen quietly asks for four times the pixels this scene was profiled at. The budget bounds that; the floor stops a very large window from scaling so far down that the board turns to mush. The HUD is unaffected.

_audio_comment: Sound is synthesised in code from noise and swept sine tones - there are no audio files in this repository. master_db is deliberately low: this is a game you play for twenty minutes at a time with four hundred shots a second going off. The *_gap_seconds values are how long each kind of sound must wait before it may play again; shots are throttled hardest because there are two orders of magnitude more of them than anything else, and a leak is not throttled at all because every one of them matters. M mutes.
